info.title: AIR Classifier
info.description:
Layered text classification with cost-aware escalation.

Three routes share one ladder and one response envelope: `/v1/sentiment` for the
base verdict on any text, `/v1/feedback` for triage (urgency, actionability,
routing), and `/v1/reviews` for aspect scoring and rating consistency.

Every request enters at the cheapest rung of a four-tier ladder — deterministic
rules, a statistical classifier, a locally served LLM, a metered cloud LLM — and
climbs only as far as the confidence, margin and complexity of the input
actually require. The rung that decided is reported as `decided_by`, and the
reasoning is in `escalation_trace`.

A rung being unavailable is not an error. When a tier fails or a provider is
down, a lower rung answers and the response carries `degraded: true` with HTTP
200. The only failure the ladder can surface is `503 no-verdict`, which means
every enabled rung declined.

Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

get.description: Reports that the process is up. Never probes tiers or dependencies.
Probes every enabled tier and the cache backend. Returns 200 for both `ok` and `degraded`; 503 only when no tier can produce a verdict.

503.description: No tier can serve; the pod should leave rotation.

get.description: What this deployment can do right now: which rungs are enabled and available, their model versions, and the request limits in force.

post.description: Runs the escalation ladder over a single text and returns the verdict, the rung that decided it, and — unless suppressed via `options.include_trace` — why the ladder climbed as far as it did.

post.summary: Analyse many texts in one call
post.description: Analyses every item concurrently, bounded by `app.batch_concurrency`. A failing item yields a problem document in its own slot while its siblings still return results, so the call is never all-or-nothing.

post.summary: Analyse one piece of user feedback
post.description: Sentiment plus triage signals for a single feedback item. `urgency`, `actionability` and `suggested_route` are deterministic heuristics computed from the verdict, a fixed cue vocabulary and the `channel` — they are not model output. Use them to order a queue, not as evidence.

Label.title: Label
Label.description:
Sentiment labels.

UNKNOWN is not a classification — it is what a tier returns when it declines
to judge, and it always escalates.

min_tier.description: Force the ladder to reach at least this rung.

max_tier.description: Hard ceiling; also a privacy and cost lever.

Options.title: Options
Options.description:
Per-request controls over the ladder.

``model_fields_set`` is load-bearing here: the API needs to distinguish
"caller explicitly asked for redact_pii=false" from "caller said nothing and
got the default", because an API key carrying ``force_pii_redaction``
rejects the former and silently permits the latter.

ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse
ReadyResponse.description:
Readiness.

``status`` is ``degraded`` — not ``not_ready`` — when an upper tier is down
but a lower one can still answer. Taking the pod out of rotation for a cloud
outage would be exactly the wrong reaction.
